mainTopic: The end of פרק אלו מציאות (משנה versus תלמוד, two דרשות about scholars) and the opening of פרק המפקיד: who gets the thief's כפל when a guardian pays
overview: This amud finishes פרק אלו מציאות and opens פרק המפקיד. First, the גמרא explains why a teaching praised תלמוד above everything and then said to run to משנה more: once the praise was taught in רבי's days, everyone left משנה, so רבי corrected them. The praise of תלמוד rests on רבי יהודה ברבי אלעאי's דרשה that a scholar's accidental mistakes count as deliberate, which matches 'הוי זהיר בתלמוד'. A second דרשה of his sorts four groups by their learning and ends with hope: all ישראל will rejoice, and only the nations will be ashamed. The new משנה rules that a free guardian who pays instead of swearing collects the thief's כפל or ארבעה וחמשה, while one who swears leaves those payments to the owner. The גמרא shows why the משנה needed both an animal and vessels. Then רמי בר חמא challenges how the owner can transfer a payment that does not exist yet, even according to רבי מאיר. His challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the teaching tells you to run to משנה
steps.stepSummary: The praise of תלמוד was taught in רבי's time. People then left משנה completely, so רבי added that one should always run to משנה more than תלמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the days of רבי this teaching was taught. Everyone left משנה and went after תלמוד. So he then taught them: always run to משנה more than to תלמוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the same teaching first praises תלמוד and then says to prefer משנה. The second line was added later, after people overreacted to the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two lines don't contradict each other. They were said at two different times for two different reasons. רבי saw that people were skipping the basics of משנה, so he pushed them back to it.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, who arranged the משנה
תלמוד: working out the reasons behind the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: 'משנה זו' here does not mean a משנה in our מסכת. It means the earlier teaching that praised תלמוד.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a lasting rule of learning. Deep analysis is great, but it can't replace knowing the basic rulings.

phrases.english: In the days of Rebbi this teaching was taught,
phrases.notes: 'This teaching' means the line just before this, which praised תלמוד above everything.

phrases.english: everyone left the Mishnah
and went after the Talmud.
So he then expounded to them:
And always run to the Mishnah
more than to the Talmud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised before this section, between praising תלמוד and preferring משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical context: the two lines were said at different times
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching seems to contradict itself, praising תלמוד and then preferring משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second line was added by רבי to correct people abandoning משנה.

steps.title: What did he expound
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which דרשה lay behind the original praise of תלמוד, the praise that made everyone leave משנה for תלמוד.
steps.whatsHappening: This short question sets up the next step. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק-based teaching was behind the praise of תלמוד that people took so seriously.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 said the praise of תלמוד was taught, and people ran after it. The גמרא now asks which פסוק-based teaching stood behind that praise.

phrases.english: What did he expound?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the praise of תלמוד mentioned in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which דרשה was the basis for praising תלמוד as the greatest kind of learning?

steps.title: Scholars' mistakes count as deliberate
steps.stepSummary: The answer is the דרשה of רבי יהודה ברבי אלעאי on 'הגד לעמי פשעם'. For תלמידי חכמים, accidental sins are treated like deliberate ones. For עמי הארץ, deliberate sins are treated like accidental ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like רבי יהודה ברבי אלעאי expounded: what does the פסוק mean, 'Tell My people their rebellious sins, and the house of יעקב their accidental sins'? 'My people, their rebellious sins' are the תלמידי חכמים, whose accidental sins become like deliberate ones. 'The house of יעקב, their accidental sins' are the עמי הארץ, whose deliberate sins become like accidental ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a דרשה that splits the פסוק into two groups of people. Each group is judged by a different standard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A learned person is expected to know better, so even his mistakes are counted as if he did them on purpose. An unlearned person is judged more gently. This is why careful study of תלמוד, which works out the reasons behind the rulings, is so important: a scholar's mistakes are held fully against him.
steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards that the scholars get the harsher word 'פשע'. That is exactly the point: more knowledge means more responsibility.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Elai expounded:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"Declare to My people their transgression
and to the house of Jacob their sins"?
phrases.notes: The פסוק uses two words for sin. 'פשע' sounds deliberate and 'חטא' sounds accidental, and the דרשה builds on that difference.

phrases.english: "Declare to My people their transgression": these are the Torah scholars,
whose accidental sins become for them like deliberate ones.
"And to the house of Jacob their sins": these are the unlearned,
whose deliberate sins become for them like accidental ones.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The דרשה on 'הגד לעמי פשעם': scholars are held to a higher standard.

steps.title: Matching משנה: be careful in Talmud
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links this דרשה to the משנה where רבי יהודה says to be careful in תלמוד, because an accidental mistake there counts as deliberate.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what we learned: רבי יהודה says, be careful in תלמוד, because an accidental mistake in תלמוד counts as deliberate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that this דרשה is the basis for a known משנה, where רבי יהודה says to be careful in תלמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The דרשה said scholars' mistakes count as deliberate. The משנה applies this to learning itself. A mistake that comes from careless תלמוד is held against you as if you did it on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what we learned (in a משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: The more you know, the more your mistakes count. That is why a scholar must be careful in his study of תלמוד.

phrases.english: And this is what we learned:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in אבות 4:13.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Be careful in Talmud,
for an accidental mistake in Talmud counts as deliberate.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the דרשה of step 3 to a known משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that a scholar's accidental sin counts as deliberate.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of רבי יהודה: 'הוי זהיר בתלמוד, ששגגת תלמוד עולה זדון'.

steps.title: Four groups in one verse
steps.stepSummary: A second דרשה of רבי יהודה ברבי אלעאי reads a פסוק as describing four groups: scholars, people of מקרא, people of משנה, and unlearned people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה ברבי אלעאי expounded: what does the פסוק mean, 'Hear the word of ה׳, those who tremble at His word'? These are the תלמידי חכמים. 'Your brothers said' are the people of מקרא. 'Who hate you' are the people of משנה. 'Who push you away' are the unlearned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another דרשה by the same רבי. It goes through the פסוק phrase by phrase and matches each phrase to a different type of person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each group relates to the scholars differently. Those who know only מקרא act like 'brothers'. Those who know משנה 'hate' them. The unlearned 'push them away'. The order runs through the same levels of learning discussed above: מקרא, משנה, and the full scholar.

keyTerms.meaning: those who push you away / shun you

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Elai expounded:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"Hear the word of the Lord,

phrases.aramaic: הַחֲרֵדִים אֶל דְּבָרוֹ״ – אֵלּוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים,
phrases.english: you who tremble at His word": these are the Torah scholars;
"your brothers [said]": these are the masters of Scripture;
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is the corrected wording, and it comes straight from the פסוק itself.

phrases.english: "who hate you": these are the masters of Mishnah;
"who push you away": these are the unlearned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new דרשה by the same רבי, on the same theme of levels of learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק in ישעיהו 66:5 describes scholars and three other groups, each relating to the scholars differently.

steps.title: The less learned groups still have hope
steps.stepSummary: The דרשה rules out the idea that the non-scholar groups have lost all hope. The words 'ונראה בשמחתכם' show that they too will see the joy.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the groups that are not scholars have lost their hope and their chance. So the פסוק says: 'That we may see your joy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The דרשה blocks a wrong conclusion someone might draw from the four groups in step 5. It says the less learned groups are not written off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 split the פסוק into scholars, people of מקרא, people of משנה, and עמי הארץ. That could sound like only the scholars count. The words 'ונראה בשמחתכם' show that everyone in ישראל will get to see and share the joy.

keyTerms.meaning: Lest you say: it sets up a possible wrong idea so it can be rejected

phrases.english: Lest you say
their hope has ended and their chances are gone?
phrases.notes: 'Their' means the groups that are not תלמידי חכמים from the previous step.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'That we may see your joy.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר פָּסַק סִבְרָם וּבָטַל סִיכּוּיָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same דרשה and heads off a harsh reading of the four-group division.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading a further phrase of the same פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The non-scholar groups are left with no hope.
steps.terutzMaskana: All ישראל will see the joy of the scholars.

steps.title: Only the nations will be ashamed
steps.stepSummary: The דרשה rules out the idea that ישראל will be ashamed. The words 'והם יבשו' refer to the nations, while ישראל will rejoice.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think ישראל will be ashamed. So the פסוק says: 'And they will be ashamed.' The nations of the world will be ashamed, and ישראל will rejoice.
steps.whatsHappening: The דרשה blocks a second wrong idea: that the shame in the פסוק falls on ישראל. It says the shame belongs to the nations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The end of the פסוק says 'they will be ashamed.' The דרשה reads 'they' as the אומות העולם, not any group of ישראל. So the whole פסוק ends with comfort for every Jew.
steps.whatToRemember: The four-group דרשה ranks people by how much they learn, but it ends on hope. Every group in ישראל shares in the joy, and only the nations are ashamed.

phrases.english: Lest you say that Israel will be ashamed?
The verse says: 'And they will be ashamed,'
the nations of the world will be ashamed
and Israel will rejoice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second 'lest you say' that finishes the דרשה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying who the pronoun in the פסוק refers to
steps.terutzMaskana: The nations are ashamed, and ישראל rejoices.

steps.title: הדרן: closing פרק אלו מציאות
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula of פרק אלו מציאות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, 'These are the found objects.'
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the second פרק of בבא מציעא. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'הדרן עלך' shows a wish to come back and learn this פרק again. The next line starts a brand-new topic.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: said when a פרק is finished
'These are the found objects': the name of the second פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'These are the found objects'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final אגדה.

steps.title: A guardian who pays instead of swearing
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה sets up the case. A free guardian lost an item to theft or loss and chose to pay the owner, even though he could have sworn and been free.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone gave an animal or utensils to a friend to watch. They were stolen or lost. The friend paid and did not want to swear, since the חכמים said: 'A שומר חנם swears and goes free.'
steps.whatsHappening: The new פרק המפקיד opens by setting up a case. The actual ruling comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר חנם is not responsible for theft or loss. He can take an oath that he was not careless and pay nothing. Here he chose to pay anyway, and that choice will matter for who gets the thief's payment.

keyTerms.meaning: One who gives an item to someone else to watch
Swears and goes free of paying

steps.confusionAlert: He was not required to pay. He could have sworn and walked away. That is why paying counts as a choice that earns him something.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who deposits with his friend
an animal or utensils,
and they were stolen or lost,
and he paid and did not want to swear,
for they said:
'An unpaid guardian swears and goes free.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמַּפְקִיד אֵצֶל חֲבֵירוֹ בְּהֵמָה אוֹ כֵלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case of a שומר חנם who paid instead of taking his oath.

steps.title: The thief's extra payment goes to the guardian
steps.stepSummary: If the thief is found, he pays כפל, or ארבעה וחמשה if he slaughtered or sold the animal. That payment goes to the guardian who paid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the thief is found, he pays double. If he slaughtered or sold the animal, he pays four or five times. To whom does he pay? To the one who had the deposit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its ruling: the thief's fine goes to the שומר who paid, not to the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the שומר paid when he did not have to, he takes the owner's place regarding the stolen item. So he collects not only the item's value but also the extra fine. The owner already got his money back.

keyTerms.meaning: Double payment that a thief must pay
Four- or fivefold payment for a stolen sheep or ox that was slaughtered or sold

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main question of the פרק: when and how a שומר who pays gains the rights to the stolen item and its fines.

phrases.english: If the thief is found –
he pays the double payment.
If he slaughtered or sold it –
phrases.notes: שמות 21:37: five for an ox, four for a sheep.

phrases.english: he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.
To whom does he pay?
To the one who had the deposit with him.
phrases.notes: He means the שומר, who already paid the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the case set up in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a שומר חנם pays instead of swearing, the thief's כפל or ארבעה וחמשה goes to the שומר.

steps.title: If the guardian swore instead of paying, the extra payment goes to the owner
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the opposite case: the guardian swore and refused to pay. When the thief is found, his כפל or ארבעה וחמשה goes to the owner of the deposit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the guardian swore and did not want to pay, and then the thief was found, the thief pays double. If he slaughtered or sold the animal, he pays four or five times. To whom does he pay? To the owner of the deposit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its case by looking at a guardian who chose to swear instead of paying. In that case, the thief's payment goes to the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 the guardian paid, so he earned the thief's extra payment. Here he did not pay; he only swore to free himself. He gave the owner nothing, so he gets nothing, and the owner keeps the right to collect from the thief.

keyTerms.meaning: He took an oath (the guardian swore it was stolen or lost without his fault)
The owner of the deposited item
Double payment that a thief must pay
Four or five times the value, paid by a thief who slaughtered or sold a stolen sheep or ox

steps.whatToRemember: Paid the owner → the guardian gets the thief's extra payment. Swore instead of paying → the owner gets it.

phrases.english: If he swore and did not want to pay,
phrases.notes: "He" is the free guardian from step 9, who swore that the item was stolen or lost.

phrases.english: and the thief is found, he pays the double payment.

phrases.aramaic: טָבַח וּמָכַר – מְשַׁלֵּם תַּשְׁלוּמֵי אַרְבָּעָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה,
phrases.english: If he slaughtered or sold it, he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.
To whom does he pay? To the owner of the deposit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite case to step 10: the guardian swore instead of paying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the guardian swore and did not pay, the thief's כפל or ארבעה וחמשה goes to the owner of the deposit.

steps.title: Why does the משנה mention both an animal and vessels?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking why the משנה needed to list both בהמה and כלים, instead of giving one general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why did the משנה need to teach the case of an animal, and why did it need to teach the case of vessels?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks why the משנה gave two examples, an animal and vessels. It is setting up a צריכותא, where it will show that each example is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה opened with someone who deposited 'an animal or vessels' (step 9). The rule seems the same for both, so one example might seem enough. The גמרא wants to know what each example adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Why did it need to teach?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Why does it need to teach an animal,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the opening words of the משנה: 'one who deposits an animal or vessels' with his friend.

phrases.english: and why does it need to teach vessels?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לֵיהּ לְמִתְנֵי בְּהֵמָה, וּלְמָה לֵיהּ לְמִתְנֵי כֵּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה's wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why both examples, an animal and vessels, are needed in the משנה.

steps.title: If only an animal were taught, we would think it is because of the bother
steps.stepSummary: Both cases are needed. If the משנה said only 'animal,' we might think the owner gives the כפל to the guardian only because caring for an animal is a lot of work. That reason does not apply to vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If it taught only an animal, I would have said: only with an animal does the owner give the double payment to the guardian, because it is a lot of work to bring it in and take it out. But with vessels, which take little work, say he does not give him the double payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer: both examples are needed. This step explains what we would have wrongly thought if the משנה mentioned only an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner gives the guardian the right to the thief's כפל as a kind of reward. With an animal, the guardian worked hard, leading it in and out, so we might think the reward is only for that hard work. Vessels just sit there, so we might think the owner would not give up the כפל. Mentioning vessels shows the rule applies to them too.

keyTerms.meaning: Both are needed (each case teaches something)
I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
He transfers to him the right to the double payment

steps.confusionAlert: The guardian does not get the כפל on his own. The idea is that the owner gives him the right to it, because the guardian paid. That is why the reason for the owner's generosity matters here.

phrases.english: They are needed, for if it had taught only an animal,
I would have said:
It is only an animal for which he transfers to him the double payment,
phrases.notes: "He" is the owner, and "him" is the guardian who paid.

phrases.english: because the work it takes is great,
to bring it in and to take it out.
But vessels, which do not take much work,
say he does not transfer to him the double payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 12 by explaining why vessels must be mentioned.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Vessels are needed, because with only an animal we would think the owner gives up the כפל only as a reward for the hard work of tending it.

steps.title: If only vessels were taught, we would think it is because the extra payment is small
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה said only 'vessels,' we might think the owner gives up the כפל only because it is a modest amount. With an animal, the thief might pay ארבעה וחמשה, so maybe the owner would not give that up. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it taught only vessels, I would have said: only with vessels does the owner give the double payment, because their double payment is not large. But with an animal, where if the thief slaughtered or sold it he pays four or five times, say the owner does not give him the double payment. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other half of its answer: what we would have wrongly thought if the משנה mentioned only vessels. It ends by saying that both cases are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With vessels, the most the thief can owe is double, so the owner does not lose much by giving it away. With an animal, the thief may owe four or five times its value, which is a big sum. We might think the owner would not give that up, so the משנה must mention an animal too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed (closing a צריכותא: each case is necessary)

steps.whatToRemember: An animal and vessels are both needed. An animal alone → we would think it is a reward for the hard work. Vessels alone → we would think it is because the extra payment is small. Together they show the guardian who pays gets the thief's extra payment in every case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer builds on the idea that the owner actively transfers his right to the thief's payment to the guardian. That idea is exactly what the גמרא will question next.

phrases.english: And if it had taught only vessels, I would have said:
It is only vessels for which he transfers to him the double payment,
because their double payment is not large,
but an animal, where if he slaughtered or sold it,
he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment,
say he does not transfer to him the double payment.
So both are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the צריכותא begun in step 13 by explaining why an animal must also be mentioned.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An animal is needed, because with only vessels we would think the owner gives up the כפל only because it is a small amount, unlike the possible ארבעה וחמשה for an animal.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both examples in the משנה are necessary; neither one could be learned from the other.

steps.title: You cannot give away something that does not exist yet
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא challenges the משנה. The owner is giving the guardian a כפל payment that does not exist yet, and a person cannot transfer something that has not come into the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא challenged this: But a person cannot transfer ownership of something that has not yet come into the world!
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא attacks the rule from Step 10. That rule said the owner lets the guardian who paid collect the thief's כפל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the guardian pays, the thief has not been caught and owes nothing yet. So the owner seems to be handing over a payment that does not exist. The general rule is that a person cannot transfer a דבר שלא בא לעולם, so how can the guardian get it?

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it (a strong objection to a statement)
An אמורא who raises the challenge
Something that does not exist yet

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not that the guardian does not deserve the money. The question is technical: how can ownership pass when the thing being given does not exist yet?

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama challenged it:
But a person cannot transfer ownership
of something that has not come into the world!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the גמרא explained why the משנה needed both בהמה and כלים, it now questions the basic mechanism of the rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the guardian who paid receives the thief's כפל or ארבעה וחמשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כפל does not exist when the guardian pays. A person cannot transfer a דבר שלא בא לעולם, so the owner cannot pass it to the guardian.

steps.title: Even רבי מאיר would not allow it here
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא strengthens his challenge. רבי מאיר allows transferring something not yet in existence, but only for things expected to come, like palm-tree fruit. 'But here' opens the contrast, which the גמרא finishes right after.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even according to רבי מאיר, who said a person can transfer something not yet in the world, that applies only to things like the fruit of a palm tree, which are likely to come. But here...
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא blocks a possible escape: maybe we follow רבי מאיר, who allows such transfers. The words 'but here' set up a contrast that the גמרא finishes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's leniency covers only things that normally come into being, like fruit that a palm tree regularly produces. רמי בר חמא is about to argue that our case is different. The explanation of why comes right after 'but here.'

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who holds that one can transfer something not yet in existence
These words apply only to... (limits a rule)
Which are likely to come into being

steps.whyThisMatters: This step narrows רבי מאיר's leniency. It covers only things that are expected to come into being, not every future item.

phrases.english: And even according to Rabbi Meir
who said a person can transfer ownership
of something that has not come into the world,
that applies only to things like fruit of a palm tree
which are likely to come,
phrases.notes: Literally, 'which are made to come,' meaning a palm tree normally produces fruit.

phrases.english: but here

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר דְּאָמַר אָדָם מַקְנֶה דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge from Step 15 by closing off the answer that we could follow רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: A possible defense of the משנה based on רבי מאיר's opinion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר allows the transfer only for things likely to come into being, like palm-tree fruit. Our case is about to be shown as different.
